verbs.description: Move a session to another directory: types `/cd <path>` and submits it. Claude Code then runs the session's tools from there, so later Bash calls stay in it, and loads that directory's project settings, MCP servers, skills and CLAUDE.md. `list_other` and the Swarm board show the session under the scope it moved to. Queues behind a running turn. Refused for a path that is not a directory, for one Claude Code is not trusted in (the trust dialog would wait on a person), and while a modal or permission prompt is showing. A worktree of an awm project is trusted first, not refused. Claude Code drops the session's MCP servers on a move, so the verb reconnects awm after it as `mcp` does; reconnect any other server with `mcp`. CLAUDE.md files add up across moves: the old one stays in context. On your own session, one follow-up prompt reports the move when it has run.

params.description: An absolute directory on this node.
params.name: path

params.description: A job id, or a session name as `list_other` shows it. Omit to act on your own session.
params.name: job

verbs.description: Compact your own conversation: injects /compact into your own prompt; it queues and runs the instant the current turn ends. A resume prompt is then injected AFTER compaction completes (a detached watcher waits for it — the resume is never queued behind /compact, so it always lands on the freshly-compacted context) so the session resumes instead of going idle. Returns immediately with followup_deferred=true. Call with no arguments; works the same in a terminal session and in a background one.

params.description: Prompt queued after /compact to resume work (default 'Continue with what you were doing.').
params.name: followup

params.description: Wait this many ms before injecting (default 0).
params.name: delay_ms

verbs.description: Set a session's effort: types `/effort <level>` and submits it. Queues behind a running turn. Refused while a modal or permission prompt is showing. Claude Code asks 'Change effort level?' when the conversation already has output; this verb answers that dialog with 'Yes, switch to <level>' (it closes it with Escape if the cursor is on No, and leaves a dialog a PreModelSwitch hook raised alone). Claude Code saves the new level as the default for new sessions; this verb puts the saved default back in ~/.claude/settings.json, and the running session keeps the new level. On your own session the command runs when your turn ends, and exactly one follow-up prompt then reports whether the change succeeded or did not apply.

params.description: low, medium or high. High is the upper limit; xhigh and max are refused on any model.
params.name: level

verbs.description: Reconnect, enable or disable a session's MCP servers: types `/mcp <action> <server>` and submits it. These forms act without opening Claude Code's MCP panel; bare `/mcp` opens it and stays refused everywhere. Queues behind a running turn. Refused while a modal or permission prompt is showing. On your own session the command runs when your turn ends, and one follow-up prompt then reports it. Claude Code records what a queued command printed only when it was submitted to an idle prompt, so that report often cannot quote it. Another session between turns answers with the printed result as `output`.

verbs.description: To talk to another agent, use your harness's own channel first: in Claude Code, `SendMessage` to a session that `ListAgents` shows, and the reply comes back the same way. Use this verb when the harness has no such channel, or to drive another session's prompt, such as a slash command. Type text into another session's prompt and submit it (no Escape, so it queues behind its current turn). Same guards as `message_self`: destructive commands need confirm, modal commands are refused, and so is a session showing a modal or permission prompt. Every /mcp line is refused: reconnect, enable or disable servers with the `mcp` verb. No follow-up is added.

params.description: A job id, or a session name as `list_other` shows it.
params.name: job

params.description: The line to type.
params.name: text

params.description: Required to send destructive commands (/clear, /quit, /exit).

verbs.description: Type a command/text into YOUR OWN prompt and submit it (no Escape, so it QUEUES behind the current turn). Use for self-directed slash commands like /compact or /model opus. Works the same whether your session runs in a terminal or as a background job — you do not need to know which. It types only into your own session; `message` types into another. A submitted slash command is auto-trailed by a follow-up prompt (override with `followup`) so the session has a next turn once the command finishes — a bare command would otherwise go idle. The follow-up is DEFERRED (injected after the command completes, never queued behind it) so it can't run ahead of the command. Modal commands (/status, /model with no arg, …) are refused — they trap input and freeze the session. So is every /mcp line: use the `mcp` verb.

params.description: The line to inject, e.g. '/compact' or '/model opus'.
params.name: text

params.description: Press Enter to submit after pasting (default true).
params.name: enter

params.description: Prompt injected after a slash command completes to keep the session alive (default 'Continue with what you were doing.'). Ignored for plain prompts.
params.name: followup

params.description: Wait this many ms before injecting (default 0).
params.name: delay_ms

params.description: Required to send destructive commands (/clear, /quit, /exit).
params.name: confirm

verbs.description: Put your own session back into bypass-permissions mode. Approving a plan drops the session into whatever mode it was in before planning — from a phone that is 'auto', where a classifier gates every action. This cycles the permission mode (the Shift+Tab cycle) until the session reads as bypass permissions, checking after each step rather than assuming a starting point. Already in bypass is a no-op. Acts only on your own session.

verbs.description: Switch a session's model: types `/model <model>` and submits it. Queues behind a running turn. Refused while a modal or permission prompt is showing. Claude Code asks 'Switch model?' when the conversation already has output; this verb answers that dialog with 'Yes, switch to <model>' (it closes it with Escape if the cursor is on No, and leaves a dialog a PreModelSwitch hook raised alone). Claude Code saves the new value as the default for new sessions; this verb puts the saved default back in ~/.claude/settings.json, and the running session keeps the new value. On your own session the command runs when your turn ends, and exactly one follow-up prompt then reports whether the change succeeded or did not apply.

verbs.description: List the deferred resumes this service still owes — one per session that has a slash command in flight. A session that compacted and then went idle forever is the visible symptom of one of these being lost; this is how you tell whether the promise is still being watched or vanished with a restart. `lost` lists the newest resumes reflection gave up on, each with its reason; each was also posted to the session's scope journal. Reports on the whole node, not just the caller.

Turn Remote Control on or off for a session on this node. On types `/rc <name>` and returns the claude.ai link once it connects, or link=null with a link_reason. Off types `/rc` and selects 'Disconnect this session' in the modal it opens; it is refused if the session is mid-turn or the modal is not the expected one. Your own session cannot answer in the same turn: the command runs when the turn ends and one follow-up prompt resumes you, carrying the link when turning on.

Start a named background Claude Code session in a scope's worktree, creating the worktree if it is absent, and return its job id and the `claude attach` command. Refuses on a station, for a caller that is not a domestic peer, when no Claude Code daemon runs, when the worktree is untrusted, or when a live session already holds the name or the scope. The new session claims its scope, and a stop ends the claim. A lobby start claims nothing until its `cd`. A worktree of an awm project is trusted first, not refused. The session defaults to skip-permissions. `model` and `effort` are required, with no default: a call without them is refused. Pick both to fit the task, a smaller model and lower effort for mechanical work, a larger model and high effort for design or debugging. High is the upper limit, so xhigh and max are refused on any model. A call that names Fable needs the user to agree first: ask in the chat. Every caller gets the same session, whoever it is.

params.description: The project the scope belongs to.
params.name: project

verbs.description: Retire a background session on this node: stop it and remove its job (`claude stop`, then `claude rm`). The transcript stays, so the session is still resumable by its session id. A retire wakes each session that waits on it (`wait`), on any node. Retiring is the last step of every finished session: one that ends its work and sits idle never wakes its waiters. Works on any session, and on a job whose session has already exited, by its job id. Your own session is refused unless confirm is true, and is then stopped after this call returns. A terminal session is refused.

params.description: A job id, or a session name as `list_other` shows it.
params.name: job

params.description: Required to stop your own session.
params.name: confirm

verbs.description: Retire a session that `start_other` created: stop it and remove its job, as `stop` does. A pinned job is unpinned first. The retire wakes each session that waits on it. Refuses a job that `start_other` did not create.

params.description: The job id `start_other` returned.
params.name: job

verbs.description: Pause your own session until every session in `until` has retired, then wake it with a line that says so. A wait works like a retire, in place of `stop`: compact first, then call it as the last step of a turn, after the sessions you hand work to have started. A background session stops and keeps its job, and the wake resumes it. A terminal session stays open and gets the line typed in. A listed session that itself waits has not finished, so nested waits hold. The wait clears when you wake, are resumed by hand, or retire.

params.description: The session ids (R9, as start_other returns them) to wait for.
params.name: until

verbs.description: Every recorded wait: who waits, on whom, which of them have retired, since when, and in which scope.
